0.0.n: A borrowed English word commonly used for a midday meal.

0.1.n: This particle shows what will be eaten.

0.2.n: 食べる loses る before に to express the purpose of going.

0.3.n: After 食べ, this particle marks eating as the purpose of going.

0.4.n: The polite form of 行く, referring here to a proposed outing.

0.5.n: At the end, this particle makes the polite sentence a question.

0.tip: 食べに行く means going somewhere to eat; the question works here as an invitation, without explicitly saying want.
